transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
My family made me come in because they're worried that I've been losing a lot of weight and barely eating. Honestly, I don't think it's a big deal, but I promised them I'd get checked out.
How do you feel about your current body weight, and do you worry a lot about gaining weight?

To be honest, I am absolutely terrified of gaining even a tiny bit of weight, and I constantly worry about the numbers on the scale going up. Even though my family says I'm too thin, when I look in the mirror, I still feel really heavy and fat. I just feel like I can't afford to put on any weight at all.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food and feel like you can't stop, or do you ever make yourself throw up or use laxatives to control your weight?
No, I never do anything like that. I don't have times where I lose control and overeat, and I've never forced myself to throw up or used laxatives.
How has your mood been lately? Have you been feeling persistently down, or have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?
My mood has been fine, honestly. I haven't really noticed any major changes or felt down lately.
Do you find yourself exercising excessively or setting very strict rules about what and when you are allowed to eat?

I don't really exercise, but I do have very strict rules about eating. I intentionally skip meals like breakfast and lunch, and I completely avoid things like carbs and fats to keep my daily calories as low as possible.

latest_inference.note: The patient meets all core DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for Anorexia Nervosa: restriction of energy intake leading to low body weight, intense fear of gaining weight, and body image distortion with lack of recognition of the severity of their low weight. Binge eating, purging, and major depressive disorder have been ruled out. Thus, the diagnosis of Anorexia Nervosa is confirmed.
